constraint: CPU core count, device memory and GPU renderer must together describe a configuration the vendor actually ships. Each field being individually legal is not sufficient.

evidence.source: capture differential: an 8-core / 16GB machine reporting an Apple Max-tier GPU. Max silicon ships at 14+ cores and 36GB minimum, so the combination is not purchasable.

evidence.note: deviceMemory rounds physical RAM to a power of two and clamps to [2,32] on desktop, so it constrains installed RAM to a range rather than naming it

notes: The characteristic failure of per-field synthesis. Replaying a real capture cannot produce it.

constraint: The GPU named by WebGL and the GPU described by WebGPU's adapter limits, architecture and feature set must be the same device.

evidence.source: capture differential: WebGL renderer changed to a newer GPU while every WebGPU adapter limit stayed byte-identical to the real hardware and architecture still read metal-3

notes: WebGPU is the second emitter most likely to be forgotten; see docs/SUBSYSTEMS.md.

constraint: The renderer string in GPUInfo and the one WebGL returns must agree.

evidence.note: GPUInfo path, GPU process
reads GL_RENDERER live through the command buffer; this is what JavaScript sees

notes: Two independent emitters. Patching only the GPUInfo one changes chrome://gpu and leaves every detector's value untouched.

constraint: Every render surface must return byte-identical output across repeated reads within a session.

evidence.source: own capture, real Chrome 152 on M4 Max: canvas, WebGL1, WebGL2 and the audio render byte-identical across two separate page loads

notes: Axiom A3 measured rather than asserted. Per-call noise violates this by construction.

constraint: An element's reported rect must agree with its computed style. Where computed style declares integer CSS coordinates, getBoundingClientRect must return exactly those coordinates; a sub-pixel offset against an integer declaration cannot arise naturally.
check: rect.x == computed.left and rect.y == computed.top for integer-positioned elements

evidence.source: own capture: real Chrome returns x=-10000, y=0 for an element at left:-10000px; top:0
capture differential: a perturbing browser returned x=-10000.015625, y=-0.03125 for the same stylesheet — offsets of 1/64 and 1/32 px

notes: Geometry noise is more identifying than the value it hides: the artifact has no natural cause.

constraint: The OS named by the UA string, navigator.platform, userAgentData and the Sec-CH-UA-Platform header must be the same OS.

evidence.source: own capture: all four agree in stock Chrome

constraint: The browser major version in the UA string, in userAgentData brands and fullVersionList, and in the Sec-CH-UA header must match. Brand list order and the GREASE entry are randomised by the engine and are not part of the constraint.

evidence.source: own capture and capture differential: both browsers were internally consistent here; order and GREASE punctuation differed between them and both are legitimate

notes: Do not treat brand order or the GREASE brand as a tell — Chrome varies both deliberately.

constraint: The difference between screen and available dimensions must be plausible window furniture for the claimed OS. The exact inset varies with dock and menu bar state and cannot be pinned to a single value.

evidence.source: own capture: 1728x1117 screen, 1728x1001 available — a 116px inset from macOS menu bar and dock
two captures of one MacBook five hours apart
evidence.note: availHeight was 1001 in one session and 1003 in the other, so the inset varies with dock state and an exact value cannot be required — only a plausible one

notes: Measured variance on real hardware is why this is a plausibility constraint rather than an equality one.

constraint: Installed fonts, speech synthesis voices, system colours and system fonts must all belong to the claimed OS.

evidence.source: own capture: 32 fonts detected and 86-entry voice list, both macOS-specific

notes: Four surfaces, one cause. Cheap to get right when the host OS matches the claim and very hard when it does not.

constraint: Timezone must be identical on the main thread, in workers, and in the browser process.
notes: Three override layers. Setting one leaves contexts disagreeing about what time it is, detectable by comparing a Date in a worker against one on the main thread.

constraint: The reported timezone must be plausible for the geographic location of the connection's exit IP.

evidence.source: follows from the claim being a whole device on a network, not two independent settings

notes: Jointly owned by subsystems 8 and 10; held by the arbiter rather than either shard.

constraint: WebRTC ICE candidates must agree with the claimed network position and must not reveal a host address inconsistent with it.

evidence.note: kWebRTCIPHandlingPolicy

notes: Jointly owned by subsystems 9 and 10.

constraint: Against an origin advertising HTTP/3, the browser must attempt QUIC wherever stock Chrome would, including when a proxy is configured.

evidence.note: QUIC is attempted only when proxy_info_.is_direct(), so a proxied session silently loses HTTP/3

notes: Why SOCKS5 UDP ASSOCIATE is a coherence requirement rather than a feature. See docs/subsystems/network-proxy.md.

constraint: The Device-Memory client hint header and navigator.deviceMemory must report the same value.

evidence.note: the same static is computed independently in the browser and renderer processes, so they can disagree

notes: Cheap for a server to check and impossible to notice from inside the renderer.

constraint: A profile should claim resources at or below what the host can satisfy. Claiming more is permitted but carries weak-evidence risk, because measured parallelism plateaus at the host's real capacity.

evidence.note: thread pools size from NumberOfProcessors, so a worker scaling curve plateaus at the host's real core count whatever the reported value says
no cgroup or CFS-quota handling anywhere in base/system/, so stock Chrome in a CPU-limited container already reports more cores than it can use — the same contradiction, with nothing spoofed

notes: Weak, not fatal. A scaling-curve probe fires on containerized, virtualized, loaded and throttled real browsers alike, so no detector can rule on it. The loader clamps and warns rather than refusing: trading a rarely-probed weak signal for a hard usability failure is the worse deal. Only two fields are host-coupled; device identity is portable.

constraint: A session configured through a proxy must remain proxied across network changes. No transport may reconnect directly to the origin.

evidence.note: Migrate() reconnects to connection()->peer_address(), so a peer address set to the origin rather than the SOCKS relay would open a direct socket to the origin on every network change

notes: Not a fingerprinting edge but a leak: the failure is silent, only occurs on network transition, and deproxies the session including the real client address. Settled in docs/subsystems/network-proxy.md by requiring the QUIC peer address to be the relay.

constraint: A canvas of flat fills must encode to approximately the size real rendering produces. Per-pixel perturbation destroys the run-length structure PNG relies on, so the encoded length inflates even though every individual pixel remains plausible.
check: len(toDataURL(flat_fill_canvas)) within expected range for the drawn content

evidence.note: a 60x30 single-colour fill encoded to 262 bytes in stock Chrome and 406 in a browser injecting canvas noise — 55% larger for identical drawing commands

notes: A passive check costing one canvas draw and a string length, needing no pixel comparison and no reference value. It detects the presence of noise rather than the identity of the device, which is why axiom A3 forbids noise outright instead of trying to make it subtle.

constraint: TextMetrics values must carry the precision real rasterisation produces. Ascent and descent at common font sizes land on exact values; a near-integer with a long fractional tail indicates a perturbed measurement rather than a measured one.
check: measureText fields match the reference exactly, including their precision

evidence.note: stock Chrome returned fontBoundingBoxAscent 13 and actualBoundingBoxAscent 15; a perturbing browser returned 13.00003373571476 and 15.000038925824724 for the same string and font

notes: Same failure as coh.layout-integer-positions in a different API: the perturbation is more identifying than the value it conceals.

constraint: Every high-entropy client hint delivered as a request header must equal the same value read from navigator.userAgentData.getHighEntropyValues() in the page it was sent for.
check: all(header['sec-ch-ua-'+h] == uaData.high[h] for h in high_entropy_hints)

evidence.note: one GetUserAgentMetadata call in the browser feeds the header path and, by mojo copy, the JS path — so in stock Chrome they cannot disagree, and any disagreement is introduced by us
two emission sites in two processes read that one struct; a patch applied at only one of them breaks this edge

evidence.source: own capture (resources/fingerprints/raw/apple-m4-max-20260907T033252Z.json): own capture: all eight high-entropy values in probes['navigator.userAgentData'].high match their headers in probes['headers.echo'] exactly

notes: The client-hints analogue of coh.device-memory-header-vs-js, and cheaper for a server to check because it needs no JavaScript at all beyond one echo.

constraint: navigator.userAgentData.platform and the Sec-CH-UA-Platform header must be the same string.

evidence.note: both read metadata.platform from GetPlatformForUAMetadata

evidence.source: own capture (resources/fingerprints/raw/apple-m4-max-20260907T033252Z.json): own capture: navigator.userAgentData.platform "macOS" and sec-ch-ua-platform "macOS"

notes: Split out from the general edge because Sec-CH-UA-Platform needs no Accept-CH opt-in: a server gets it on the very first request, before scripts run, so this pair is checkable on a bare page load.

constraint: The brand list in navigator.userAgentData.brands and the Sec-CH-UA header must contain the same brand/version pairs in the same order, including the GREASE entry.

evidence.note: the header is a structured-header serialisation of the same brand_version_list vector the JS accessor copies, so order is preserved rather than coincidental

evidence.source: own capture (resources/fingerprints/raw/apple-m4-max-20260907T033252Z.json): own capture: brands [Chromium 152, Not?A_Brand 24, Google Chrome 152] and sec-ch-ua "Chromium";v="152", "Not?A_Brand";v="24", "Google Chrome";v="152" — same entries, same order

notes: Order is randomised across versions but not across surfaces within one browser. coh.ua-version-agreement correctly says order is not a tell when comparing two browsers; this edge says order must still be identical between the header and the JS value of the SAME browser, which is a different claim and does hold.

constraint: The brand-list permutation and the GREASE brand and version are deterministic functions of the claimed browser major version, so a profile claiming version N must present the list Chromium N would generate, not a list captured from a different version.

evidence.note: GetRandomOrder indexes a fixed permutation table by seed % 6 (or % 24), the GREASE brand picks punctuation by seed % 11 and (seed+1) % 11 from an 11-entry table, and the GREASE version is {"8","99","24"}[seed % 3] — the seed is the major version number, and no RNG is involved anywhere

evidence.source: own capture (resources/fingerprints/raw/apple-m4-max-20260907T033252Z.json): own capture, derived from source for seed=152: 152%11=9 gives '?', 153%11=10 gives '_', so "Not?A_Brand"; 152%3=2 gives "24"; 152%6=2 selects permutation {1,0,2} giving [Chromium, Not?A_Brand, Google Chrome]. The measured list is byte-identical to the derivation.

notes: Deliberately weak severity: this does NOT reintroduce brand order or GREASE as a detection signal, and coh.ua-version-agreement's rule that neither is a tell stands. It is a constraint on our own generator — the fields are not free parameters, so replaying a captured brand list beside a different claimed version manufactures a value stock Chrome never produces. A detector would need our source to spot it, which is why it is weak rather than fatal.

constraint: The Accept-Language request header and navigator.languages must describe the same ordered language list, allowing for the header's q-value expansion.

evidence.note: one pref, two independent transforms, delivered to two different processes — the renderer gets a bare comma list through RendererPreferences, the network service gets an expanded q-value string through GenerateAcceptLanguageHeader

evidence.source: own capture (resources/fingerprints/raw/apple-m4-max-20260907T033252Z.json): own capture: Accept-Language "en-US,en;q=0.9" on the wire against navigator.languages ["en-US","en"]

notes: Structurally the same failure as coh.device-memory-header-vs-js and just as invisible from inside the renderer. Note the comparison must strip q-values and account for ExpandLanguageList adding base languages, so a naive string equality check produces false positives.

constraint: The navigator language list, the Accept-Language header and the locale resolved by Intl must name a consistent locale for the claimed device.

evidence.note: when the accept-languages pref is empty Blink falls back to Platform::Current()->DefaultLocale(), the host UI locale — so an unset profile value silently leaks the real machine locale into navigator.language

evidence.source: own capture (resources/fingerprints/raw/apple-m4-max-20260907T033252Z.json): own capture: navigator.language "en-US", Accept-Language "en-US,en;q=0.9", Intl locale "en-US" — all agree while the timezone is Asia/Bangkok, which is a legitimate combination and must not be flagged

notes: Jointly owned with subsystem 8. Deliberately does not constrain locale against timezone: T0 shows a real device with en-US and Asia/Bangkok, so treating a locale/timezone mismatch as a tell would fire on real travellers and expatriates.

constraint: The User-Agent request header and navigator.userAgent must be byte-identical.

evidence.note: three writers in three processes, all reading embedder_support::GetUserAgent(); patching one leaves the others on the build's real string

evidence.source: own capture (resources/fingerprints/raw/apple-m4-max-20260907T033252Z.json): own capture: the wire User-Agent and probes['navigator.scalars'].value.userAgent are identical strings

notes: The browser writes the navigation header before a renderer for that document exists, so a Blink-side patch cannot cover the first request even if it makes every later one agree.

constraint: navigator.appVersion must equal navigator.userAgent with the leading "Mozilla/" removed.

evidence.note: appVersion is agent.substr(agent.find('/') + 1); the relation holds by construction in stock Chrome and can only be broken by a patch

evidence.source: own capture (resources/fingerprints/raw/apple-m4-max-20260907T033252Z.json): own capture: appVersion is exactly userAgent minus "Mozilla/"

notes: Cheap, decisive, and the classic casualty of a patch that overrides accessors one at a time instead of the emitter.

constraint: The mobile bit, the form-factor list and the presence of a "Mobile" token in the UA string must all describe the same class of device.
check: uaData.mobile == (header['sec-ch-ua-mobile'] == '?1') and form_factors == (['Mobile'] if uaData.mobile else ['Desktop']) and ('Mobile' in navigator.userAgent) == uaData.mobile

evidence.note: one switch, --use-mobile-user-agent, drives the mobile bit, the derived form-factor list and the " Mobile" product suffix; they are not independent fields

evidence.source: own capture (resources/fingerprints/raw/apple-m4-max-20260907T033252Z.json): own capture: mobile false, form factors ["Desktop"], no "Mobile" token in the UA string

notes: Setting the mobile bit alone is never a complete change, and it also pulls in maxTouchPoints and screen geometry from subsystem 4.

constraint: The frozen engine constants must match the engine the UA string claims: a Chromium UA requires productSub "20030107" and vendor "Google Inc.".
check: navigator.productSub == '20030107' and navigator.vendor == 'Google Inc.' if 'Chrome/' in navigator.userAgent else True

evidence.note: both are literals; Gecko returns productSub "20100101" and an empty vendor, so the pair identifies the engine independently of the UA string

evidence.source: own capture (resources/fingerprints/raw/apple-m4-max-20260907T033252Z.json): own capture: productSub "20030107", vendor "Google Inc." beside a Chrome/152 UA

notes: Free to satisfy by leaving both alone. Recorded because it is the check that catches a UA string edited without touching the engine.

constraint: navigator.pdfViewerEnabled must be true exactly when navigator.plugins holds the five spec-fixed PDF entries, and false exactly when it is empty.

evidence.note: the constructor fills the array only when IsPdfViewerAvailable() is true, and pdfViewerEnabled calls the same function — one bit, two observables, no intermediate state

evidence.source: own capture (resources/fingerprints/raw/apple-m4-max-20260907T033252Z.json): own capture: pdfViewerEnabled true with the five-entry fixed plugin list

notes: Jointly relevant to subsystem 11. Any patch that fabricates a plugin list without going through this bit produces a combination the code cannot generate.

constraint: The UA string must not contain the "Headless" product token, and the brand list must contain the browser brand the UA claims.
check: 'Headless' not in navigator.userAgent and any(b.brand == claimed_brand for b in uaData.brands)

evidence.note: the --headless switch inserts "Headless" into the product token inside GetUserAgentInternal, upstream of every consumer, so it reaches the UA string, the header and appVersion together
the browser brand entry is compiled in only under #if !BUILDFLAG(CHROMIUM_BRANDING); a Chromium-branded build emits a two-entry brand list with no "Google Chrome", which no Chrome corpus row matches
brand is set only under #if !BUILDFLAG(CHROMIUM_BRANDING), so a Chromium build emits a brand list with no browser entry — a two-line patch, not a build blocker
GetUserAgentInternal inserts "Headless" into the product token when the --headless switch is present, upstream of every consumer

notes: Arbiter correction: the shard recorded both halves as build-configuration failures unreachable by an emitter patch. Both are reachable, and are now ordinary spoof rows. The brand entry is suppressed by an #if guard that a patch can simply drop, and the Headless token is inserted by a single command-line check in GetUserAgentInternal. Neither requires is_chrome_branded or src-internal. The edge itself stands as the invariant both patches must satisfy.

constraint: HDR is a single display property with four web-visible faces and they must agree: screen.colorDepth is 30 exactly when (color: 10) matches, exactly when (dynamic-range: high) matches, and — because an HDR colour space short-circuits the gamut computation to P3 — an HDR display can never report color-gamut srgb only. The SDR case is the mirror: colorDepth 24, (color: 8), dynamic-range standard only.
check: (colorDepth == 30) == (css.color == 10) == matchMedia('(dynamic-range: high)').matches and not (colorDepth == 30 and gamut == ['srgb'])

evidence.note: Display::SetDisplayColorSpacesRef derives color_depth and depth_per_component from color_spaces->SupportsHDR() — one input, two outputs
the platform sets 30/10 or 24/8 from the same enable_hdr boolean that installs the extended-sRGB output colour space
IsHDR() short-circuits the gamut to P3 before any primaries are examined
colorDepth 30, pixelDepth 30, color 10, dynamic-range ['standard','high'], color-gamut ['srgb','p3'] — all four faces of one HDR display, measured together

notes: Four surfaces, one cause, and the cheapest coherence check in this subsystem: three matchMedia calls and one property read. Any patch that writes screen.colorDepth without moving the display colour space fails it immediately. Also couples to the GPU subsystem — render_widget_host_impl.cc:1063-1069 strips HDR when hardware acceleration is off, so an HDR profile and software rendering are mutually exclusive.

constraint: The DPR client hint on the navigation request, the DPR client hint on subresource requests, window.devicePixelRatio and the CSS resolution media feature must all report the same ratio.

evidence.note: the navigation header is computed in the browser process from its own display list and host zoom map, with no renderer involvement
the subresource header is computed in the renderer from LocalFrame::DevicePixelRatio, the same function window.devicePixelRatio forwards to
dpr: 2 on the wire against window.devicePixelRatio 2 in stock Chrome

notes: The direct analogue of coh.device-memory-header-vs-js, and the reason this subsystem's device scale factor patch has to land in the browser process. Note the two producers already differ in stock Chrome on a multi-monitor host, because the browser uses the primary display and the renderer uses the window's display — so the edge is only reliably checkable for a single-display profile, which is the case the corpus covers.

constraint: window.devicePixelRatio and the CSS resolution / -webkit-device-pixel-ratio media features must return the same number to full float precision, and both must scale with page zoom.

evidence.note: both are one-line forwarders to LocalFrame::DevicePixelRatio, so in stock Chrome they cannot disagree
the shared value is device_scale_factor x page zoom x css zoom, so it is not constant across zoom levels

notes: Zero-cost for a detector: a binary search over (min-resolution: Xdppx) recovers the float without reading the property, so wrapping or hiding window.devicePixelRatio accomplishes nothing. The second half of the constraint matters as much as the first — a patch that returns a fixed number makes the ratio stop responding to zoom, which is a behaviour no real browser has.

constraint: screen.width x devicePixelRatio and screen.height x devicePixelRatio must be a panel resolution the claimed hardware actually ships, in the same sense that coh.hardware-product-configuration requires a purchasable machine.

evidence.note: 1728 x 2 = 3456 and 1117 x 2 = 2234, which is the 16-inch MacBook Pro panel exactly; the logical size alone would not have shown this
bounds and backingScaleFactor are read from the same NSScreen, so the product is by construction the real panel on real hardware

notes: Catches the characteristic per-field synthesis error: a plausible logical size paired with a plausible scale factor whose product is not a display anyone manufactures. Marked strong rather than fatal because scaled display modes on macOS produce logical sizes whose product is a rendering target rather than the panel, so the check needs the profile's model to rule.

constraint: screen.orientation.type must be the landscape family when screen.width >= screen.height and the portrait family otherwise, and screen.orientation.angle must be 0 for the primary orientation of an unrotated desktop display.

evidence.note: GetOrientationTypeForDesktop classifies from `bounds.height() >= bounds.width()` and the panel rotation angle; the type is derived from the bounds, not stored beside them
1728x1117 with type landscape-primary and angle 0

notes: Free if the bounds are patched at DisplayUtil::DisplayToScreenInfo, because the type is computed from them there. Broken instantly by a patch applied only to Screen::width()/height(), which is the point of recording it.

constraint: The CSS device-width and device-height media features must equal screen.width and screen.height.

evidence.note: both read ScreenInfo::rect through ChromeClient, so in stock Chrome they are the same two integers

notes: The cheap check that catches a patch applied to the Screen accessor instead of to ScreenInfo. A few dozen matchMedia calls recover device-width by binary search without touching the screen object at all.

constraint: The window rect must lie inside the claimed available rect: screenX >= availLeft, screenY >= availTop, screenX + outerWidth <= availLeft + availWidth, and screenY + outerHeight <= availTop + availHeight. Negative screen coordinates are impossible for a single-display profile.
check: screenX >= availLeft and screenY >= availTop and screenX + outerWidth <= availLeft + availWidth and screenY + outerHeight <= availTop + availHeight

evidence.note: screenX 0 == availLeft 0, screenY 33 == availTop 33, outerHeight 1000 <= availHeight 1001, outerWidth 1728 == availWidth 1728 — the window sits flush inside the work area

the window rect and the available rect reach the renderer over two different mojo channels from two different browser-side sources, so nothing in Chromium enforces this relation once the screen values are spoofed

notes: This is why window.outer-dimensions and window.screen-position are inherit rather than spoof: the requirement is a relation the profile loader satisfies by placing and sizing the real OS window, not a value to write. It also imposes a hard usability constraint that mirrors coh.claim-within-host-capacity — a profile claiming a display smaller than the host's cannot be run maximised, and a profile claiming one larger than the host's can never fill it. The loader should clamp the launch window rather than let arithmetic that cannot hold ship.

constraint: outerHeight - innerHeight is the height of the browser's own chrome and outerWidth - innerWidth is its horizontal frame plus any classic scrollbar. Both deltas are platform-specific and must match the claimed OS.

evidence.note: outerHeight 1000 - innerHeight 913 = 87px of vertical chrome, and outerWidth 1728 - innerWidth 1728 = 0px horizontally — macOS has no window side frame and uses overlay scrollbars
outer comes from the OS window rect and inner from the layout view size, so the difference is the real browser furniture and is produced by the platform, not by any value we can set

notes: The screen-geometry analogue of coh.platform-resource-sets: a macOS profile served from a Windows host contradicts itself in this subtraction with no screen value patched at all, because Windows adds horizontal window frame and a 15-17px classic scrollbar that macOS does not have. Marked strong rather than fatal because the vertical delta legitimately varies with the bookmarks bar, extensions and downloads shelf, so only the horizontal delta and the coarse magnitude are reliable. Cheap to satisfy when host OS and claimed OS agree; not fixable inside this subsystem when they do not.

constraint: The Viewport-Width / Sec-CH-Viewport-Width header must equal window.innerWidth, and Sec-CH-Viewport-Height must equal window.innerHeight, for requests made from that document.

evidence.note: viewport-width 1728 on the wire against window.innerWidth 1728

subresource requests take the value from LocalFrameView::ViewportWidth in the renderer while navigation requests take it from view->GetVisibleViewportSize() in the browser, divided by two different zoom sources

notes: Strong rather than fatal because the navigation header is necessarily stale relative to the document it loads — it describes the viewport before layout. The check is only decisive against subresource requests, where the same process produced both numbers.

constraint: screen.isExtended false requires that getScreenDetails() enumerate exactly one screen and that the window's screen coordinates lie within that one screen's rect.
check: not screen.isExtended implies len(screenDetails.screens) == 1 and window_within(screenDetails.screens[0])

evidence.note: is_extended is GetNumDisplays() > 1 while getScreenDetails enumerates the ScreenInfos list built by GetScreenInfosNearestDisplay — the same display list, read two ways, so flipping one boolean does not shorten the other
isExtended false with screenX 0 and screenY 33, inside the single 1728x1117 screen

notes: Depends on screen.details, which is currently escalated for lack of corpus coverage, so this edge cannot close until the collector gains a getScreenDetails probe. Recorded now because it settles how screen.is-extended must be patched: shorten the ScreenInfos list, do not flip the flag.
